claims.text: The driver's own 'arrived' tap at 09:39:14 was false: the trip record shows the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 09:39:16, but the GPS trace shows the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 09:41:14 — 120 seconds after the marker. Under POL-NS-05 the arrival marker does not start the waiting clock; the clock is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix.

On the recomputed clock the driver's in-geofence dwell was only 210 seconds, from 09:41:14 to 09:44:44, against a required minimum dwell of 300 seconds for a STANDARD zone class — a shortfall of 30 seconds. The cancellation fee is therefore not chargeable and must be refunded in full under POL-NS-06.

The driver's own counterparty statement concedes the false marker: 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' That admission, read with the 120-second gap between the tap and the first in-geofence fix, confirms the arrival marker was premature and cannot start the waiting clock under POL-NS-05.

The rider was not a no-show in any meaningful sense: the rider's device was stationary within the rider-presence radius throughout the waiting window (mean distance 637 m from the pin, all fixes at 0.0 km/h), and the rider's track shows 63 fixes from 09:36:37 to 09:45:52. The rider was present and stationary; the driver cancelled at 09:44:46 while the rider was still there.

The driver's single chat message 'im at the pickup point' was sent at 09:39:34, 20 seconds after the false arrival tap, and the rider read it at 09:40:04. The driver then cancelled at 09:44:46 without any further coordination. The driver's own message is inconsistent with his position: the GPS trace places him outside the arrival radius at that time.

The fare breakdown confirms the rider was charged SGD 4.50 as a cancellation fee, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The full amount contested is SGD 4.50, and the rider seeks its return.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road: EV-ADVIS-02749-01 is MISSING with a BLOCKING issue. Under POL-NS-06(i) a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the accumulation limb unavailable, so the driver cannot rely on it to extend or excuse the shortfall. The absence is itself citable.

The driver's profile shows one no-show termination in the trailing 30 days against 75 completed trips — a rate of 0.013, well below the 0.08 anti-farming threshold, and the absolute count is below 4. The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip, so the case does not escalate on that ground; but equally, the driver's compensation is not payable because the fee itself is not chargeable under POL-NS-06.

The rider's profile shows zero no-show disputes in the trailing 30 days, zero disputes with this counterparty in 90 days, and zero prior no-show flags. There is no pattern of abuse on the rider's side, and no ground for escalation under POL-NS-09(c) or (d).

The GPS trace is COMPLETE with 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps, and both driver and rider tracks present. The admissibility pre-pass assigns weight 1.0. The deciding facts — the 210-second dwell and the 30-second shortfall — rest on clean, unimpaired evidence, so the confidence floor of 0.70 is comfortably met and no escalation under POL-NS-09(a) or (e) is warranted.

claims.text: The driver's own trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 210 seconds, from 09:41:14 to 09:44:44, with 22 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied on the recomputed clock and the arrival is not a fiction.

The driver's in-geofence dwell of 210 seconds exceeds the free waiting period in force for this trip, 180 seconds under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met and the waiting period the rider paid for was actually served.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 09:44:46 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed at 09:44:44, and the record shows no boarding event — POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on its face.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:39:14, which is 120 seconds BEFORE the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 09:41:14 (dwell_start_offset_sec = -120.0). That marker is early, but POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit that a false marker does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell nonetheless meets the minimum — and here it does, at 210 seconds against 180. The fee stands; the early tap is a referral item only.

The rider's own track is present and clean (63 fixes, 100% coverage) and places the rider's device at a mean distance of 637 m from the pickup pin, with a minimum of 634 m — far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider_presence_radius_m — and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. The rider was not at the pickup point during the waiting window.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider here: limb (a) fails because the only chat message in the log was sent BY THE DRIVER ('im at the pickup point', 09:39:34), not by the rider, and the rider sent nothing locating or coordinating during the waiting window. The rider-contact clause simply does not engage.

POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes are INSIDE the 50 m arrival radius, not outside it but within 400 m. The wrong-entrance clause is confined to drivers stationary outside the arrival radius, so it neither refunds the rider nor diverts the fee to a pin-ambiguity goodwill payment.

POL-NS-06 does not rescue the rider either. The measured dwell of 210 seconds is not shorter than the 180 second minimum — the shortfall_sec figure of -30.0 confirms the dwell EXCEEDS the minimum by 30 seconds — so the waiting-period-shortfall clause has no work to do.

The driver's own statement is a candid admission that he pressed 'arrived' a bit early, but he also states he waited at the pin — and the trace corroborates the waiting: 22 qualifying in-geofence fixes over 210 continuous seconds. The admission of an early tap is not an admission of non-arrival.

The fare ledger is clean and reconciles: the cancellation fee line is SGD 4.50, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50, and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. There is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect to disturb the charge.

The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does NOT trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, which is below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 75 is 0.013, well below the 0.08 rate limb. Both limbs are required and neither holds, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

Compensation is therefore due at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force, which the fare ledger computes as driver_compensation of SGD 3.60, the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The driver drove to Pasir Ris, waited out the full free period, and the ruling should say so in cash.

The missing traffic advisory does not help the rider: EV-ADVIS-02749-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, and POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated advisory before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed. Here there is only ONE in-geofence interval anyway (run_count = 1), so the limb is unavailable and unnecessary — the single 210 second run already clears the minimum.

The rider's claim that 'the app said the driver arrived when he was still far away' is true only of the 09:39:14 button tap, not of the arrival itself. The trace shows the driver reached the pin at 09:41:14 and held there for 210 seconds; the rider's own device sat 637 m away throughout. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: you are right that the app told you the driver had arrived when he had not, and that finding is recorded — but it does not return your SGD 4.50, and here is why. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:39:14, while the GPS trace shows his first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup radius only at 09:41:14, 120 seconds later, and the driver's own statement concedes he 'pressed arrived a bit early'. Under POL-NS-05 that arrival marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock; the clock is recomputed to run from 09:41:14. On that corrected clock the driver did serve the period your fee pays for: he held position inside the radius continuously for 210 seconds, from 09:41:14 to 09:44:44 (22 qualifying fixes), and cancelled at 09:44:46, which is 212 seconds after the recomputed clock began. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (fee_schedule.defaults agrees). POL-NS-05 limb (iii) provides that an early marker does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum, and here it exceeds it by 30 seconds — the trace's own shortfall figure is -30.0. Your POL-NS-06 shortfall argument, that the required dwell is 300 seconds because the zone class is STANDARD, is rejected: the 300-second figure is fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec, and that fee schedule's resolution rule states minimum_dwell_sec is retained only to interpret records authored before policy version 2 and is never applied to a record that carries its own platform_policy. This trip record does carry one, and it fixes the period at 180 seconds. (Your own arithmetic would also give a 90-second gap, not the 30 seconds the claim states.) All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold on the recomputed basis: (a) the arrived event exists; (b) the driver was in-geofence from 09:41:14, the start of the recomputed clock; (c) the 210-second dwell exceeds the 180-second free waiting period (no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies); and (d) the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:44:46 under RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event, after the required dwell elapsed. POL-NS-03 does not apply because the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it; POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you because you sent no locating or coordinating message during the waiting window (the only chat message, at 09:39:34, is the driver's) and your track places your device 634 to 640 m from the pin, outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, with zero qualifying fixes. To the driver: the early tap was a real defect and it is recorded as a false-arrival referral under POL-NS-05(iii), but the fee itself stands. Your POL-NS-07 compensation is payable: the anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the required 4, and 1 divided by 75 completed trips is 0.013, below the 0.08 rate limb), so you receive 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force — SGD 3.60, as computed in the fare ledger's money block — the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The rider's charge of SGD 4.50 therefore stands unchanged, and the amount this ruling moves is SGD 3.60. On confidence and escalation: the deciding facts (the 210-second in-geofence dwell and the recomputed clock) are carried by the GPS trace EV-GPS-02749 and the trip record EV-TRIP-02749, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and my confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; no limb of POL-NS-08 is met (no clock skew over 90 seconds, no trace gap over 120 seconds, chat sequence and count intact, the SGD 4.50 fee line matches platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd), and no ground of POL-NS-09 arises, so no escalation is warranted. POL-NS-09(b) does not fire because POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves the tension between the 09:39:14 marker and the 09:41:14 in-geofence fix. The monetary effect of SGD 3.60 does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so this provisional ruling executes on issue. Finally, for disclosure: two claims about the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02749-01 were discarded at the citation stage for citing that artifact without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code, and both parties' framing of POL-NS-06 limb (i) is in any event moot — there is only one in-geofence interval (run_count = 1), so no accumulation is required.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this NO_SHOW_CHARGE dispute concerns the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee. The fee was validly charged, the charge stands, and the driver is owed SGD 3.60.

What happened. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:39:14, and DRV-09749 candidly concedes he 'pressed arrived a bit early'. That is right: the GPS trace carries no in-geofence fix at or before the tap, and its first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius is at 09:41:14 — 120 seconds later (dwell_start_offset_sec = -120.0), while the recorded track shows the driver still on the approach at travelling speeds. Under POL-NS-05 the arrival marker is FALSE and does not start the waiting clock.

The recomputed outcome. The clock is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 09:41:14. The driver held position inside the arrival radius for 210 continuous seconds (09:41:14 to 09:44:44, 22 qualifying fixes), against the free waiting period in force for this trip of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). POL-NS-05(iii) therefore applies: an early marker does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell still meets the minimum, and POL-NS-01 governs — its limb (b) being read from the recomputed clock. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold: (a) the trip record carries the driver 'arrived' event; (b) the trace places him in the geofence from 09:41:14 on the recomputed clock; (c) he dwelled 210 s, which is at least the 180 s free waiting period; and (d) he terminated at 09:44:46 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell elapsed at 09:44:44. POL-NS-02 is independently met by 22 qualifying in-radius fixes.

The rider's claims. Your account that the app announced the driver while he was still out on the main road is correct about the marker — that is exactly why a false-arrival record goes into the referrals — but it does not make the fee unchargeable: the driver did reach the pin and did serve the full waiting period, and POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit that an early tap does not void an otherwise good fee. Your POL-NS-06 shortfall claim is rejected: you measured against a 300-second minimum, but 300 s is fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec, which the resolution rule retains only for records authored before policy version 2 and never applies to a record that carries platform_policy. The in-force minimum is the free waiting period of 180 seconds, and the 210-second dwell exceeds it by 30 seconds, so there is no shortfall and POL-NS-06 has no work to do. Your POL-NS-04 claim is rejected: limb (a) fails because the only chat message in the log was sent by the driver, not by you, and your own track places your device at a mean distance of 637 m from the pin (minimum 634 m) with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, so limb (c) fails as well. POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it but within 400 m.

ruling.explanation: Addressed to both parties. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. Facts. The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 09:39:14 was early, and he concedes it. The platform started the 180-second free-wait timer at 09:39:16, but the driver's first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius is at 09:41:14 - 120 seconds after the tap (EV-GPS-02749, dwell_start_offset_sec -120.0; EV-TRIP-02749). Under POL-NS-05 that marker is a false arrival marker: it does not start the waiting clock, and the clock is recomputed to run from 09:41:14. On the recomputed clock the driver held position inside the geofence continuously for 210 seconds, 09:41:14 to 09:44:44, across 22 qualifying fixes, and cancelled at 09:44:46 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW; no boarding event is recorded (EV-GPS-02749; EV-TRIP-02749). Rider's arguments. Your central point - that the dwell falls 30 seconds short of a 300-second STANDARD minimum - fails on the figures. The minimum is the free waiting period in force under POL-NS-01(c), read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec: 180 seconds. The 300-second minimum_dwell_sec in the fee schedule is a legacy figure retained only to interpret records authored before policy version 2 and is not applied to a record that carries platform_policy. Your 210-second dwell exceeds 180 seconds by 30 seconds (EV-GPS-02749, shortfall_sec -30.0), so POL-NS-06 gives you no refund. Your second point, that the rider's device was inside the rider-presence radius, is contradicted by your own track: it sits about 637 m from the pin throughout (minimum 634 m), outside the 100 m STANDARD radius, with no qualifying in-radius fix (EV-GPS-02749). POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you either: limb (a) needs a rider message, and the only chat message in the log was sent by the driver (EV-CHAT-02749). POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it. Driver. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold: the arrival event is in the trip record; the trace places you in the geofence on the recomputed clock; you served the free waiting period; and you terminated the trip for RIDER_NO_SHOW after the dwell elapsed, with no boarding. The charge of SGD 4.50 stands - the fare ledger shows SGD 4.50, reconciling with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd 4.50 (EV-FARE-02749). The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1 divided by 75 completed trips is 0.013 (below 0.08), so both limbs fail and compensation is payable. Under POL-NS-07 that is 80 percent of SGD 4.50 = SGD 3.60, the figure the ledger computes; on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling the amount moved is that same SGD 3.60, and the rider's charge stands. Escalation. None applies under POL-NS-09: confidence is above 0.70, no admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence once POL-NS-05 resolves the marker, neither profile shows the repeat-dispute or anti-farming counts, and the deciding evidence is unimpaired. Confidence 0.90. Every deciding fact rests on artifacts at weight 1.0 - EV-GPS-02749, EV-TRIP-02749, EV-FARE-02749 and EV-DPROF-02749 - so the cap is 1.0. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02749-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries nothing here: it bears only on POL-NS-06(i)'s accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals, and there is a single interval. The monetary effect of SGD 3.60 is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes on issue.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02749 stands, and the driver is entitled to SGD 3.60 of it as compensation.

To the rider: you are right that the app told you the driver had arrived before he was at the pin. The trip record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:39:14 (EV-TRIP-02749), but the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02749) shows his first qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup geofence only at 09:41:14, 120 seconds later (dwell_start_offset_sec = -120). The driver himself concedes he pressed arrived early. Under POL-NS-05 that marker is a false arrival, it does not start the waiting clock, and it is recorded against the driver in the referrals.

That does not return your money, however. POL-NS-05 recomputes the waiting clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and the trace then shows the driver held position inside the geofence continuously for 210 seconds (09:41:14 to 09:44:44, 22 qualifying fixes). The free waiting period in force is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The 300-second minimum your submission relies on is rejected: fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec is retained only to interpret records authored before policy version 2 and, by fee_schedule.resolution_rule, is never applied to a record that carries platform_policy. The GPS-derived shortfall of -30.0 seconds confirms the 210-second dwell exceeds the 180-second minimum by 30 seconds, so POL-NS-06 (waiting-period shortfall) is not engaged — there is no shortfall to refund. POL-NS-05(iii) then applies: an early marker does not defeat the fee where the corrected dwell meets the minimum.

POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full. (a) The trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event. (b) On the recomputed clock the driver was inside the geofence from 09:41:14. (c) The dwell of 210 s exceeds the 180 s free waiting period, and no no_show_threshold_sec is set for this trip. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 09:44:46 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell elapsed at 09:44:14, and no boarding event is recorded.

No other route displaces the fee. POL-NS-03 does not apply — the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m arrival radius, not outside it within 400 m. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider: the only chat message in the log was sent by the driver (EV-CHAT-02749, 09:39:34), and the rider track (EV-GPS-02749) places the rider's device about 637 m from the pin throughout (rider_qualifying_fix_count 0). POL-NS-10 does not apply because the rider did not cancel.

To the driver: the fee stands and POL-NS-07 fixes your payout. 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee is SGD 3.60, as the fare ledger computes it (EV-FARE-02749, derived.money.driver_compensation = 3.60; the residual 20 percent is the platform service fee). The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the absolute threshold of 4, and 1/75 = 0.013, below the 0.08 rate limb, so compensation is paid rather than withheld.

Ruling: DRIVER_COMPENSATION. Per POL-GEN-03, amount_sgd carries the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd, SGD 3.60; the charge the rider paid stands as it is. No clause produces a rider refund or any other referral. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it executes automatically.

Confidence: every fact this ruling rests on is carried by EV-GPS-02749 and EV-TRIP-02749, each with weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is stated at 0.85. No POL-NS-09 escalation ground applies: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, POL-NS-05 resolves the apparent conflict between the arrival tap and the trace, and neither profile shows the POL-NS-09(c) or (d) pattern.

Claims addressed: the two traffic-advisory claims were discarded by the referee because EV-ADVIS-02749-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and the impairment was not disclosed; in any event no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) is needed because there is only one in-geofence interval (run_count = 1). The rider's claim resting on rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is discarded — that lifetime counter is CONTEXT ONLY under POL-GEN-01 and is not the field POL-NS-09(d) reads (rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d). The rider's claim of a 300-second minimum is rejected on the merits as explained above.

The corrected dwell of 210 s still met the 180 s free waiting period, so the early marker does not change the fee, but it is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver for human review and for the POL-NS-07 pattern check.

ledger.claim: The driver's own 'arrived' tap at 09:39:14 was false: the trip record shows the free waiting period of 180 seconds started at 09:39:16, but the GPS trace shows the driver's first qualifying in-geofence fix only at 09:41:14 — 120 seconds after the marker. Under POL-NS-05 the arrival marker does not start the waiting clock; the clock is recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix.

On the recomputed clock the driver's in-geofence dwell was only 210 seconds, from 09:41:14 to 09:44:44, against a required minimum dwell of 300 seconds for a STANDARD zone class — a shortfall of 30 seconds. The cancellation fee is therefore not chargeable and must be refunded in full under POL-NS-06.

The driver's own counterparty statement concedes the false marker: 'I pressed arrived a bit early but I did wait at the pin.' That admission, read with the 120-second gap between the tap and the first in-geofence fix, confirms the arrival marker was premature and cannot start the waiting clock under POL-NS-05.

The rider was not a no-show in any meaningful sense: the rider's device was stationary within the rider-presence radius throughout the waiting window (mean distance 637 m from the pin, all fixes at 0.0 km/h), and the rider's track shows 63 fixes from 09:36:37 to 09:45:52. The rider was present and stationary; the driver cancelled at 09:44:46 while the rider was still there.

The driver's single chat message 'im at the pickup point' was sent at 09:39:34, 20 seconds after the false arrival tap, and the rider read it at 09:40:04. The driver then cancelled at 09:44:46 without any further coordination. The driver's own message is inconsistent with his position: the GPS trace places him outside the arrival radius at that time.

The fare breakdown confirms the rider was charged SGD 4.50 as a cancellation fee, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The full amount contested is SGD 4.50, and the rider seeks its return.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road: EV-ADVIS-02749-01 is MISSING with a BLOCKING issue. Under POL-NS-06(i) a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the accumulation limb unavailable, so the driver cannot rely on it to extend or excuse the shortfall. The absence is itself citable.

ledger.claim: The driver's profile shows one no-show termination in the trailing 30 days against 75 completed trips — a rate of 0.013, well below the 0.08 anti-farming threshold, and the absolute count is below 4. The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip, so the case does not escalate on that ground; but equally, the driver's compensation is not payable because the fee itself is not chargeable under POL-NS-06.

The rider's profile shows zero no-show disputes in the trailing 30 days, zero disputes with this counterparty in 90 days, and zero prior no-show flags. There is no pattern of abuse on the rider's side, and no ground for escalation under POL-NS-09(c) or (d).

The GPS trace is COMPLETE with 100% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps, and both driver and rider tracks present. The admissibility pre-pass assigns weight 1.0. The deciding facts — the 210-second dwell and the 30-second shortfall — rest on clean, unimpaired evidence, so the confidence floor of 0.70 is comfortably met and no escalation under POL-NS-09(a) or (e) is warranted.

The driver's own trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 210 seconds, from 09:41:14 to 09:44:44, with 22 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-01 limb (b) is satisfied on the recomputed clock and the arrival is not a fiction.

The driver's in-geofence dwell of 210 seconds exceeds the free waiting period in force for this trip, 180 seconds under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met and the waiting period the rider paid for was actually served.

The trip was terminated by the driver at 09:44:46 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed at 09:44:44, and the record shows no boarding event — POL-NS-01 limb (d) is satisfied on its face.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:39:14, which is 120 seconds BEFORE the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 09:41:14 (dwell_start_offset_sec = -120.0). That marker is early, but POL-NS-05(iii) is explicit that a false marker does not by itself defeat the fee where the corrected dwell nonetheless meets the minimum — and here it does, at 210 seconds against 180. The fee stands; the early tap is a referral item only.

The rider's own track is present and clean (63 fixes, 100% coverage) and places the rider's device at a mean distance of 637 m from the pickup pin, with a minimum of 634 m — far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider_presence_radius_m — and rider_qualifying_fix_count is 0. The rider was not at the pickup point during the waiting window.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider here: limb (a) fails because the only chat message in the log was sent BY THE DRIVER ('im at the pickup point', 09:39:34), not by the rider, and the rider sent nothing locating or coordinating during the waiting window. The rider-contact clause simply does not engage.

POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes are INSIDE the 50 m arrival radius, not outside it but within 400 m. The wrong-entrance clause is confined to drivers stationary outside the arrival radius, so it neither refunds the rider nor diverts the fee to a pin-ambiguity goodwill payment.

POL-NS-06 does not rescue the rider either. The measured dwell of 210 seconds is not shorter than the 180 second minimum — the shortfall_sec figure of -30.0 confirms the dwell EXCEEDS the minimum by 30 seconds — so the waiting-period-shortfall clause has no work to do.

The driver's own statement is a candid admission that he pressed 'arrived' a bit early, but he also states he waited at the pin — and the trace corroborates the waiting: 22 qualifying in-geofence fixes over 210 continuous seconds. The admission of an early tap is not an admission of non-arrival.

The fare ledger is clean and reconciles: the cancellation fee line is SGD 4.50, matching platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50, and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. There is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect to disturb the charge.

The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does NOT trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, which is below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 75 is 0.013, well below the 0.08 rate limb. Both limbs are required and neither holds, so compensation is payable rather than withheld.

Compensation is therefore due at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee in force, which the fare ledger computes as driver_compensation of SGD 3.60, the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee. The driver drove to Pasir Ris, waited out the full free period, and the ruling should say so in cash.

The missing traffic advisory does not help the rider: EV-ADVIS-02749-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, and POL-NS-06(i) requires a present and populated advisory before separate in-geofence intervals may be summed. Here there is only ONE in-geofence interval anyway (run_count = 1), so the limb is unavailable and unnecessary — the single 210 second run already clears the minimum.
